claim: P0 amendment G ADOPTED by operator ruling: when a stored file's NAME misleads about its CONTENT and the file is cited by content digest so that renaming would strand those citations, add a sibling MARKER FILE beside it naming the discrepancy, the correct file and the citing rule. The bar is demonstrated harm, not tidiness -- a marker is written only where the name has caused a wrong citation or been shown capable of causing one, because a marker beside every imperfect name decays into noise the next reader learns to skip. jimbo_p1152.png cleared the bar twice: CT-S15 attributed folio-1153 transcriptions to 1152, and CT-S46 route P would have reported the paper's eq:jimbo UNVERIFIABLE against its cited page had it trusted the filename -- a false finding against correct prose. S16-R18-02 carries label PROVEN (read from its label field, at CT-S16-MEMBERSHIP-C/claims.jsonl line 24) and its claim text states one quantity twice: the unfactored z(4pqt - 4pq - 4pt + 4p + q^3 t^2 - q^3 - 2 q^2 t^2 + 2 q^2 + q t^2 - q)/4, which is correct, and the factored -z(q-1)(t-1)(4p + q^2 t + q^2 - qt - q)/4, which is not: the two differ by exactly a sign, and CT-S47's check_r18_sign.py reports 'the claim's own two forms agree: False' and 'PLUS one quarter of the same product reproduces it: True'. Both forms are present in the claim text and both were read from it (checks R4-b, R4-c), so this is a defect in the RECORD, not only in appendixA.tex's typeset display. The control R4c fires.

claim: RULING, recorded: the label on S16-R18-02 stays PROVEN, and the reasoning is the substance. A label grades whether the RESULT is proved, not whether every transcription of it is typographically correct. S16-R18-02's unfactored form is right and its factored form wrong, so the proof stands and the artefact was defective; downgrading would assert that the mathematics was in doubt, which it was not. The general statement, which this pass is what found: A LABEL IS A VERDICT ON A RESULT; IT HAS NEVER BEEN A GUARANTEE ABOUT THE BYTES OF ITS STATEMENT. The correct instrument is therefore supersession, not relabelling -- S47-12 records the corrected display under supersedes: S16-R18-02 with the original standing unedited. This bears on how much a label can be asked to carry, and is the argument for the formula pass having existed at all: no label, at any strength, would have caught it.
label: STRUCTURAL

claim: INSTRUMENT DEFECT, found and repaired in this session. Check R3-f -- 'the marker states the rule' -- FAILED on its first run against a marker that states the rule perfectly well. Cause: the needle was a literal single-space string, and the sentence 'Resolve these images by hash, never by filename.' is LINE-WRAPPED in the README between 'hash,' and 'never'. This is S43-12 recurring: a check that matches raw text with a single-space needle cannot see a phrase broken at a line end, and reports absence identical to the absence it exists to detect. Diagnosed against the raw file before anything was edited, so a correct marker was not 'repaired'. Fixed in the READER, by compiling each needle to a regex joining its whitespace-separated tokens with \\s+, and given a control requiring that the same wrap-tolerant needle does NOT match the rule stated BACKWARDS -- without which a needle loose enough to cross line breaks might be loose enough to match anything. Final state: 18 checks, 0 FAILED; 6 controls, 6 FIRED.
label: VERIFIED

claim: The PREREG advance prediction was right in its location and wrong in its mechanism, and is recorded as such rather than quietly reconciled. PREREG section 5 predicted a clean run and named R3 as the most likely place to fail, because the marker records digests as 16-hex PREFIXES followed by an ellipsis and a reader comparing full 64-hex digests would report absence for a file the marker names. R3 is indeed where the run failed -- but at R3-f, on line wrapping, not at R3-c/d/e on digest width; the prefix comparison had been built as the PREREG said it would be and passed. A prediction that names the right block for the wrong reason is a partial hit, and calling it a hit would overstate what foresight bought.
label: STRUCTURAL
